newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX off two percent at start after Dow fall.
newsitem.headline: German DAX off two percent at start after Dow fall.

text.p: Germany's DAX index on Monday fell some two percent at the start of bourse trade on Monday following Wall Street's sharp drop on Friday with continuing U.S. inflationary and interest rate fears.
The DAX-30 index of leading German shares traded 67.30 points, or 2.01 percent, lower at 3,272.75 in early dealings, with June DAX futures 44.5 points lower at 3,273.0.
Dealers said the strong dollar and steady Bunds were lending some support but all attention was now on whether the Dow can recover some of its losses when it reopens later today.
"We are all looking to see how much Wall Street can salvage from (Friday's) wreckage later on -- that will be the determining factor," said one Frankfurt-based equity salesman.
The dollar traded at 1.7225/30 marks, comfortably above the 1.72 threshold seen by many market players last week as noteworthy.
In the DAX index, dealers said that now the 3,300-point support level had been broken, there was little in the way of real support, technical or psychological, until 3,200 points.
"The market these days goes through the small-scale support levels (in between) like a knife through butter," one said.

Very few stocks managed to buck the downward trend. Drugs and chemicals group Merck could only add 10 pfennigs to 67.40 marks after publishing new sales data showing a first quarter gain of 12.4 percent to 1,896 million marks.
Even the rally that car-maker Volkswagen has seen after last week's positive 1997 outlook statement was halted, with its shares off 15.50 marks to 1,057.0.
Software group SAP, whose shares are often subject to large swings, fell 4.10 percent to 274.30.
Other loss-makers were spread widely across the market, including particularly chemical stocks and the financial sector.
